There’s no free trial either, and now I understand why. If people could see how bad the app is before paying, they probably wouldn’t subscribe. The ads make it look like it creates realistic, high-quality AI videos, but the actual results are terrible. It distorts your face so badly that the videos are basically unusable.

Charging $15 every single week for only two poor-quality videos is outrageous. Maybe if it were $15 a month it would be somewhat understandable, but a weekly subscription for this level of quality feels extremely misleading. Total waste of money.

reviews.title: Poor quality
reviews.text:
I was very disappointed with this AI Video app. The advertising makes it sound simple: just upload a photo and the AI will generate the video content you choose. Unfortunately, the reality is very different.
The biggest issue is that the generated videos don’t look anything like the actual people in the photos. I tried creating videos of myself and my wife, and neither of us looked recognizable in the final results.
Another frustrating aspect is the pricing. The app charges a weekly subscription fee, which already seems expensive. However, after subscribing, I discovered that many features are still restricted unless you purchase additional coins. These coins are not cheap, so the real cost ends up being much higher than expected.
In my opinion, the app is misleading about both its capabilities and its pricing structure. If you’re considering downloading it, make sure you understand all the extra costs before signing up. Think twice before spending your money.

reviews.title: Terrible video
reviews.text:
I was very disappointed with the AI video results. The videos looked terrible and did not resemble the quality shown in the advertisements. I was also unable to provide a detailed description of what I wanted, which greatly limited the outcome.

In one video, I was somehow dancing inside a car, which looked very strange and unrealistic. In another, the Colombian flag was floating in midair, making the scene look unnatural and awkward. Neither video was usable.

To make matters worse, I lost my points after generating these videos and now I am unable to create new ones. Unfortunately, the final results did not come close to matching the examples or expectations set by the advertisement. Overall, this was a very frustrating experience and I hope improvements are made to both the quality of the videos and the ability to customize prompts.

reviews.title: Frustrating free trial: limited access and gimmicks
reviews.text:
I recently signed up for the seven-day free trial of the app, hoping to explore its features before committing to a paid subscription. However, I was disappointed to find that the trial experience is severely limited. 

While the idea of a free trial is to provide full access to the app, I quickly discovered that I could only upload two videos. After that, I was prompted to purchase additional coins to continue using the app during my trial period. This feels counterintuitive—how can I get a true sense of the app if my usage is restricted? 

To make matters worse, I was informed that I would have to wait an astonishing 167 hours for my coins to refill, which is not only frustrating but also a significant barrier to exploring the app effectively. 

In short, if you’re considering this app, be wary of the limitations imposed during the free trial. It feels more like a gimmick than a genuine opportunity to evaluate the service. I definitely wouldn’t recommend it based on my experience.
